Doctor: Could you please provide your gender and describe the nature, location, and duration of your back pain? Patient: I'm a female, and the pain is on the right side of my back. Doctor: Have you experienced any numbness, tingling, or weakness in your legs or feet since the injury? Patient: No, I haven't had any numbness, tingling, or weakness in my legs or feet since the injury. The pain stays in my back, mostly on the right side, and it's been bothering me more when I twist or lie flat. Doctor: Have you experienced any swelling, bruising, or difficulty moving your back or legs since the injury? Patient: No, I haven't had any swelling or bruising, and I can still move my legs, though twisting my back makes it hurt more. It's been uncomfortable, but I haven't had trouble moving my legs. Doctor: Have you experienced any radiation of pain to your legs or any numbness, tingling, or weakness in your legs or feet since the injury? Patient: No, I haven't had any radiation of pain to my legs or any numbness, tingling, or weakness in my legs or feet since the injury. The pain stays in my back, mostly on the right side, and it's been bothering me more when I twist or lie flat. Doctor: Have you had any prior imaging studies, such as X-rays, MRI, or CT scans, of your spine or back, either for this injury or for any other reason? Patient: I had a fusion done on my back before, but I don't remember if there were any other imaging studies.
